newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BP busy on special dividend speculation.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BP busy on special dividend speculation.

text.p: British Petroleum stock options were active on Wednesday as traders considered yesterday's full year results from the company, dealers said.

The main deals were dividend related in which an options position was taken against a stock position. "There has been speculation that BP will make a special dividend and this has fuelled trading in the options market," said one dealer.

One such deal was the purchase of 2,000 April 650 puts at 10p against buying two million shares at 700p. This is a way of collecting the dividend but offers protection if the share price declines substantially because the value of the puts will rise.
If BP shares go up, the maximum loss will be the 10p from the long puts.
By 1450 GMT, BP shares were up 3p to 697p.
Over in mobile phone company Orange the main trade was from a buyer of 1,650 March 240 calls at 3p. There was also a buyer of 500 March 180 calls at 38p.
And in National Westminster Bank there was a seller of a total of 1,000 April 850 calls at prices of 15p and 20p.
Selling call options will produce a profit if the underlying shares fall or stay below the strike price at expiry.

But if the seller also owns stock, the short calls will provide some protection if the share price falls. And if the share price rises above the strike price there is a risk of losing the stockholding owing to assignment of the calls.
NatWest shares dipped a penny to 827-1/2p. The bank will announce full year results on February 25.
